extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers, industrialists, economists, and policymakers (readers of political economy)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on analyzing and organising manufacturing processes: how the division of labour, capital, machinery, and cost accounting determine factory size, process priorities, and pricing. Includes concrete rules for printing and publishing costs, payment systems, and incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of labour matches skill to process
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of the division of labour ... is, that it enables us to purchase and apply to each process precisely that quantity of skill and knowledge which is required for it : we avoid employing any part of the time of a man who can get eight or ten shillings a day ... in turning a wheel, which can be done for sixpence a day; and we equally avoid the loss arising from the employment of an accomplished mathematician in performing the lowest processes of arithmetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the principle to avoid overpaying skilled labour for simple tasks and to allocate the precise amount of skill required to each process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of labour requires sufficient demand and capital
rubrics_metrics.description: The division of labour cannot be successfully practised unless there exists a great demand for its produce; and it requires larger capital to be employed in those arts in which it is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before subdividing tasks extensively, ensure market demand and available capital justify specialization; watchmaking example (100+ branches) illustrates deep specialization only viable with demand and capital.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the precise expense of every process
rubrics_metrics.description: It is of great importance to know the precise expense of every process, as well as of the wear and tear of machinery which is due to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed process-level accounting informs improvement priorities, distribution, and policy decisions (e.g., taxation effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct improvements to processes that most affect total cost
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the first advantages which suggests itself as likely to arise from a correct analysis ... is the indication which it furnishes of the course in which improvement should be directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: reducing time for fixing pin heads by 1/4 reduces overall cost ~13%, whereas halving time for spinning coil barely affects total cost. Focus on high-impact subprocesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context matters: cost structure differs by technology and labour price
rubrics_metrics.description: The expense of manufacturing, in a country where the machinery is of the rudest kind, and manual labour is very cheap, is curiously exhibited ... (Java cotton example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare process-cost percentages across contexts; what matters in one economy may be negligible in another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for wear-and-tear and fixed vs circulating capital when evaluating machinery
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction of machinery ... tended to increase the quantity produced, and to lead to the establishment of large factories. The possessor ... was unable ... to compete with the old methods ... from the large capital invested in the machinery; but with continuous operation and small addition to circulating capital, profits arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute break-even considering continuous operation, maintenance, attendants, and required circulating capital; machines may require 24-hour use to be economical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange number of workers as multiples of process counts
rubrics_metrics.description: To conduct an establishment for pin-making most profitably, the number of persons employed must be a multiple of ten ... when the number of processes into which it is most advantageous to divide it is ascertained, ... all other manufactories which do not employ a direct multiple of this number, will produce the article at a greater cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan workforce size to match process-parallelism to avoid idle or misallocated labour; ratios may vary with factory size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locate successive processes together when material handling is costly or risky
rubrics_metrics.description: The material ... must, in the several stages of its progress, be conveyed from one operator to the next in succession : this can be done at least expense when they are all working in the same establishment. If the material is heavy, this reason acts with additional force; ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep interconnected processes under one roof when transport cost or damage risk outweighs benefits of decentralisation; cottage-based work possible only where quality and complete utilisation can be ensured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ resident skilled workers for machine maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the good performance and the duration of machines depend ... upon correcting ... every shake or imperfection ... it will soon become apparent that a workman resident on the spot will reduce the expenditure arising from the wear and tear of the machinery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use on-site skilled staff to promptly adjust/repair machines; economies of scale determine when it's worthwhile (single machine vs many).

rubrics_metrics.name: Size factories to match maintenance labour requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: It ought to consist of such a number of machines as shall occupy the whole time of one workman in keeping them in order, and in making any casual repairs: if it is extended beyond this, ... the necessity of doubling or tripling the number of machines ... to employ the whole time of two or three skilful workmen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose machine counts per skilled mechanic to maximise utilisation of maintenance labour and minimise per-unit upkeep costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use power (e.g., steam) to multiply labour productivity but respect material limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the loom ... were driven by a steam-engine, the same man might attend to two or more looms at once ... the steam-engine can drive the looms twice as fast as human force ... limit depended upon the strength of the thread, ... an improvement was made ... increased the speed from 100 to about 120 strokes per minute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisation can increase throughput per worker but must consider material/technical limits and implement gradual velocity improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factory expansions create ancillary needs (lighting, engineers, accountants)
rubrics_metrics.description: The factory becomes gradually so enlarged, that the expense of lighting during the night amounts to a considerable sum ... it will have been found necessary to establish an accountant's department, with clerks to pay the workmen, and to see that they arrive at their stated times; and this department must be in communication with the agents who purchase the raw produce, and with those who sell the manufactured article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate overheads and supporting departments as scale increases; capital investment decisions should include these recurring costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design payment systems to align workers' interests with factory success
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be of great importance, if, in every large establishment, the modes of paying the different persons employed could be so arranged, that each should derive advantage from the success of the whole, and that the profits of the individuals should advance as the factory itself produced profit, without the necessity of making any change in the wages agreed upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider profit-sharing, contracting, or piece-rate mechanisms to motivate productivity and care; such systems are difficult but valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contracting/tribute systems to incentivize extractive and variable-output work
rubrics_metrics.description: In the mines of Cornwall almost the whole of the operations ... are contracted for. ... 2. Tribute, which is payment for raising and dressing the ore, by means of a certain part of its value when merchantable. The miners, who are to be paid in proportion to the richness of the vein, ... naturally become quick-sighted in the discovery of ore, and in estimating its value; and it is their interest to avail themselves of every improvement that can bring it more cheaply to market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When output quality/quantity varies, tie pay to output value (tribute) to stimulate discovery and efficiency; expect income variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyse marginal impact of time/cost reductions per subprocess
rubrics_metrics.description: If any method should be contrived of diminishing by one fourth the time required for fixing on the heads of the pins, the expense of making them would be reduced about thirteen per cent., whilst a reduction of one half the time employed in spinning the coil of wire ... would scarcely make any sensible difference in the cost of the manufacture of the whole article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform marginal analysis to prioritise R&D and process improvements where they yield greatest whole-product cost savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimise waste and exploit by-products through vertical integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Amongst the causes which tend to the cheap production ... may be mentioned, the care which is taken to allow no part of the raw produce ... to be absolutely wasted. An attention to this circumstance sometimes causes the union of two trades in one factory ... (horn example with six distinct uses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and monetise co-products and waste streams; consider merging complementary trades to capture value from by-products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large manufacturers can eliminate middle-men via reputation and scale
rubrics_metrics.description: A class of middle-men, who were formerly interposed between the maker and the merchant, now no longer exist. ... the merchant, in dealing with the great manufacturer, is saved from the expense of verification, by knowing that the loss, or even the impeachment, of the manufacturer's character, would be attended with greater pecuniary detriment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage scale and reputational capital to reduce transaction costs and verification overhead with buyers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breach of product quality/trust causes severe reputational and commercial loss
rubrics_metrics.description: We brought with us ... nearly a hundred thousand needles ... 'Whitechapel Sharps' warranted 'superfine, and not to cut in the eye.' ... a number were returned ... with a complaint that they were all eyeless ... to save our credit we have been obliged to throw them away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise consistent quality control; reputational failure can force disposal of stock and incur heavy indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing/composition charges depend on type size, table-work, and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: The printer usually charges for composition by the sheet, supposing the type to be all of one kind; ... If there are a few extracts ... which require to be printed in smaller type ... a small additional price per sheet allowed. If any work with irregular lines and many figures ... it is called table-work, and is charged at an advanced price per sheet. If the page consists entirely of figures ... the charge for composition is usually doubled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When estimating publishing costs, itemise composition by sheet, add premiums for small type, table-work, pages of figures, and similar special requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author corrections are costly; prefer finalised manuscript and slips
rubrics_metrics.description: The charge for corrections and alterations ... gives rise to the greatest inconvenience. If the author study economy, he should make the whole of his corrections in the manuscript, and should copy it out fairly ... If the printer possess a sufficient stock of type, it will contribute ... to have his whole work put up in what are technically called slips and then to make all the corrections, and to have as few revises as he can.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimise post-typesetting corrections; use slips and consolidate revises to reduce correction charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-work pricing conventions: charged per 250 sheets with economies of scale
rubrics_metrics.description: The press-work, or printing off, is charged at a price agreed upon for each two hundred and fifty sheets; and any broken number is still considered as two hundred and fifty. When a large edition is required, the price for two hundred and fifty is reduced; thus ... two hundred and fifty copies ... would have been charged eleven shillings per sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for standard lot-size pricing and negotiate tiered rates; small print runs can be disproportionately expensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper excise duties and advertising taxes distort production and information flows
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of the excise duty is to render the paper thin ... they pay, not merely the duty which is charged, but also the profit on that duty ... The charge for advertisements ... as it is considered that advertisements in newspapers ... pays a duty of 3s. 6d., nearly one half of the charge of advertising is a tax. ... every tax on communicating information respecting articles ... is one which must considerably reduce the amount that would have been raised had no impediment been placed in the way of making known to the public their qualities and their price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the incidence of consumption taxes and advertisement duties in pricing strategies and policy assessments; taxes on information are particularly distortive.
